scope: Whole-board routing quality assessed from final native geometry and independently measured before/after lengths
baselineReference: Source23 campaign mean supplied in BRIEF; not an invented earlier vote from this role
geometryAcceptance: Pass: zero measured foreign electrical contacts and zero declared copper, all-net drill, width, ownership, NPTH or edge failures
improvements: Worst foreign via copper gap improves from 0.154204 mm to 0.175000 mm while all four layers are checked.
Inner1 signal length falls from 327.930 mm to 289.687 mm, improving ground-plane continuity.
Settled bypass, compensation, LOW and fan copper is shorter while native net ownership and minimum widths pass.
remainingWeaknesses: Some foreign via copper remains below the preferred 0.20 mm margin, although above the declared 0.15 mm requirement.
Multiple trace-to-pad and via-to-trace gaps remain at exactly 0.20 mm; this is valid nominal geometry with little extra spacing margin.
There are 434 full-through vias and roughly 4.04 m of planar trace; overall detours and layer transfers remain substantial.
The fan input feed remains approximately 82 mm and UART TX approximately 56 mm. These are improved or valid but still long.
reasonForScore: The changes measurably improve local power/control routing and reduce ground-plane slots, with complete native clearance validation. Remaining density, long trunks and spacing at policy floors prevent a 9/10 judgment.
limitations: Ideal CAD geometry and engineering judgment only. This rating does not establish fabrication tolerance, converter stability, EMI behavior or bench performance.
